title: The wizard's valuables
summary: One level in R.E.P.O. is built around a wizard's school, and its loot follows that theme: a broom, an hourglass and a staff are each named as their own kind of valuable rather than being ordinary props.
body: Valuables are not all the same kind of object. The wizard level's things are named in the game's own data as separate kinds of valuable, which is why they behave as loot rather than as scenery you walk past.
A broom is one of them. The game names a broom as a valuable in its own right, so it can be picked up, thrown into the cart and sold with the rest of the haul.
An hourglass is another. There is a valuable for the wizard's time glass, and the game ships a colour texture for it: that texture is the first image beside this entry.

A staff is the third one the game names. The wizard's staff is its own kind of valuable as well, which matters because the level is also full of props that look expensive but are not named as loot at all.

The level holds more wizard objects than those three. The game ships artwork for a cube of knowledge, a goblin head, a sword and a power crystal, and the files also group a set of small wizard valuables together, so the themed loot is wider than the three kinds named above.

What that means in practice: what you can carry is decided by what the game names, not by what looks valuable, and the wizard level is where that difference is easiest to see. If you are unsure whether something is loot, the test is whether it can be picked up.
What this entry does not tell you: what any wizard valuable is worth, how many of them appear in a run, or how often the level comes up. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The broom is a valuable of its own kind rather than scenery.
The wizard's time glass is a valuable of its own kind.
The wizard's staff is a valuable of its own kind.
The game ships artwork for a cube of knowledge, a goblin head, a sword and a power crystal.
